rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a controlled pre-oxidation treatment on Q235 steel, while the hidden target applies an AlCoCrFeNi HEA coating via atmospheric plasma spraying on SS316L. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (surface oxidation vs. coating deposition).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses chloride-rich solutions at 25°C and 80°C, whereas the target uses 3.5 wt% H2SO4 for electrochemical testing and 900°C cyclic hot-corrosion with Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 salt mixtures. The environments and temperature regimes are entirely different.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a barrier oxide film inhibiting chloride ingress to reduce pitting. The target mechanism involves grain refinement, BCC phase strengthening, high-entropy sluggish diffusion, and formation of specific Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides to resist sulphide/vanadate attack and hot corrosion. These are different mechanism classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower corrosion rates and pitting in chloride solutions. The target predicts and reports higher microhardness, improved electrochemical polarization resistance in H2SO4, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain at 900°C. The properties and test environments differ completely.
